input_fingerprints: fixtures are built in the test file itself: a two neuron continuous model (1 edge, delay 1) and a three neuron LIF model (3 edges, one delayed, adaptation and slow homeostasis on). No external data file is read.
observed_result: Three separately versioned artefact kinds now exist, each with its own envelope, SHA-256 payload checksum, strict decoding, required-field walk and exclusive-hardlink publication. (1) Model package, coimnet-model-package/v1: topology fingerprint (node count, edge count, SHA-256 of every source index followed by every target index, each a little-endian uint32), the complete learning.Config, the base learning.Parameters, declared units, the caller's evidence path list and the artefact schema versions it can seed. It contains no persistent neural state, no optimizer moments, no update count and no data cursor. (2) Individual snapshot, coimnet-individual-checkpoint/v1: adds the persistent neural state of whichever core is configured (for LIF: voltage, synaptic history, adaptation, refractory counters and, when declared, the rate estimate and threshold offset), the optimizer options, the Adam moments and the update count. It contains no data seed and no sample cursor. (3) Episode training checkpoint, coimnet-episode-checkpoint/v1: the complete learning.TrainingSnapshot plus the delayed-pulse-splitmix64-v1 data seed and sample cursor. It contains no persistent neural state. All six cross loads are refused with a message that names the kind the reader actually opened, and the model package refusal additionally says what a package is and what to do instead, because it is the one kind that could be mistaken for a complete recovery source. Observed messages: LoadIndividual on a package -> '"coimnet-model-package/v1" is a model package, which declares configuration and parameters only and is not an individual snapshot: seed a new individual with NewIndividualFromPackage instead of restoring one'; LoadIndividual on an episode checkpoint -> '"coimnet-episode-checkpoint/v1" is an episode training checkpoint, which carries no persistent neural state, and is not an individual snapshot'; LoadModelPackage on an individual snapshot -> '"coimnet-individual-checkpoint/v1" is an individual snapshot, which carries persistent neural state and optimizer moments, not a model package'; LoadModelPackage on an episode checkpoint -> '"coimnet-episode-checkpoint/v1" is an episode training checkpoint, which carries trainer state and a data cursor, not a model package'; Load on a package -> 'unsupported checkpoint schema "coimnet-model-package/v1"'; Load on an individual snapshot -> 'unsupported checkpoint schema "coimnet-individual-checkpoint/v1"'. Round trip and determinism: for both cores a saved package reads back reflect.DeepEqual to the in-memory package, two saves of the same package produce byte-identical files, resaving what was loaded reproduces those same bytes, no null appears in a published document, and mutating the loaded value does not affect a later load. Refusals on load, all 23 cases: a flipped payload byte, a zeroed checksum, a short checksum, a truncated document, a future envelope schema, a future payload schema, a changed fingerprint digest, a changed fingerprint edge count, a changed fingerprint node count, a missing units block, a missing time-constant unit, an empty time-step unit, a missing evidence registry, a missing compatible-versions block, an unknown compatible individual version, an absolute evidence path, an evidence path with a .. segment, a null array element, missing parameters, a parameter shape that disagrees with the configuration, an unknown field, a duplicate key and trailing data; the untampered fixture loads in the same test, so those refusals are not vacuous. Publication: a canceled save publishes nothing and leaves no temporary file, a second save to the same path fails without changing the published bytes, an empty path and a zero-value package are refused. Seeding: NewIndividualFromPackage(pkg, options, initial) produces an individual whose snapshot is reflect.DeepEqual to learning.NewIndividual with the same configuration, parameters, options and initial voltage, for a continuous model and for a LIF model with slow homeostasis enabled; their Advance outputs and their state after Advance are identical, and mutating the package afterwards does not change the individual it produced. Fingerprint encoding: the one-edge fixture hashes to 01acecb507abfe1a354aa8064f4af5d3f1acd019e37db3c11c97523b71c76e9d, which is the SHA-256 of the eight bytes 00 00 00 00 01 00 00 00 computed independently outside Go, and the test recomputes every fixture digest with a separate naive encoder; reordering the same edge set changes the digest, so the fingerprint identifies the stored edge arrays rather than the abstract graph. Cross-process exact resume (STA-03 scope): a LIF individual seeded from a saved package is advanced for four steps, trained for two episodes with the threshold group trainable, and snapshotted; a genuinely new process (exec of the test binary, guarded by COIMNET_MODEL_PACKAGE_HELPER) loads that snapshot, advances the five step tail and saves the result. The resumed snapshot is reflect.DeepEqual to the uninterrupted run in every part, including the neural state with its rate estimate and threshold offset, the parameters, the Adam first and second moments, the per-parameter step counts and the update count, and the tail readouts match value for value. The test refuses to be vacuous: it asserts the update count is 2, that training actually moved the parameters away from the package's, that at least one Adam moment is nonzero, that the resumed threshold offset is nonzero (observed [0.3748046875, 0.4, 0.0445312500000001], with neuron 1 sitting on the declared h_max 0.4) and that the compared window contains a spike.

limitations: Fixture only. Both models are hand-built test fixtures of two and three neurons; nothing here is a real-connectome, whole-graph or biological claim, and no package was built from a MaleCNS graph.

The training snapshot's completeness is scoped to what the trainer actually has. No replay store, teacher signal, fast weights, chemical state or RNG stream exists anywhere in the framework yet, so 'complete' means parameters, optimizer options, Adam moments, per-parameter step counts, update count, and for the episode format the data seed and sample cursor. STA-03 therefore stays specified: it additionally requires fast weights and chemical state, which do not exist.
The model package carries no data-provider cursor by design, so a package alone cannot resume a training job; that is the individual snapshot's and the episode checkpoint's role.

The topology fingerprint is asserted to share simulate's encoding by the documented rule plus an independent recomputation in the test, not by calling simulate's own (unexported) implementation. The two implementations could drift without a test noticing.

Load on a model package and on an individual snapshot is refused by the pre-existing schema check in checkpoint.go, which names the kind through its schema string rather than through a sentence; checkpoint.go was outside this stage's file ownership and was not changed.

Evidence registry paths are stored verbatim and checked only for being relative and not escaping (no leading slash, no backslash, no .. segment). The framework never opens them and does not verify that the records exist or describe this model.
Executed on macOS arm64 (go1.26.5) only; no Ubuntu or Windows run is recorded for this requirement.

The recorded green run was produced in an isolated copy of the working tree with a concurrent agent's unfinished ticket 17 files removed and learning/ restored to commit 32a72fd, because those files did not compile at that moment. Every ticket 16 test also passes in the shared tree itself (21 of 21), where the only failure is that agent's own unimplemented red test.
